profile.reading:
This building, TX22, is located at 5207 Rogers Road in the Westover Hills area of San Antonio, TX, on the same parcel as the neighboring TX21 building also tracked in this registry. Vantage does not publish this campus on its own site at all, so this entry relies on secondary sourcing: Data Center Dynamics reporting on the building permit. TX22 covers approximately 214,525 square feet across two stories, at a stated construction cost of roughly $272 million, with a permit timeline running from October 2025 to June 2027. No power/MW figure is disclosed in any source found, and no certifications are published, consistent with the building's pre-construction status.

Vantage acquired 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023 for its Westover Hills sub-campus, home to TX21 and TX22, separate from the Texas Research Park sub-campus (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12). This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt, 3.7-million-square-foot, 1,200-acre development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025 to meet AI demand.

San Antonio's data center growth, including Vantage's TX cluster, has concentrated on the city's West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has courted large industrial and data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rate agreements. Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have both offered property-tax abatement agreements to data center developers as part of a broader economic-diversification push beyond the city's traditional military and tourism base. CPS Energy's long-range integrated resource planning has specifically flagged data centers as a fast-growing large-load category requiring new generation and transmission investment through the early 2030s, a dynamic Texas's ERCOT grid operator has also cited statewide as it revises long-term demand forecasts upward and weighs new large-load interconnection rules for data centers.

reading.body:
Vantage Data Centers TX22 is a 214,525-square-foot building under construction in San Antonio's Westover Hills area, located on a 31-acre campus shared with the neighboring TX21 facility. The building permit, filed in October 2025 with completion targeted for June 2027, lists a construction cost of roughly $272 million, but Vantage publishes no IT capacity figure for this site. Without a disclosed power allocation, the campus's relevance to AI scaling cannot be quantified from available sources.

The Westover Hills campus sits in Bexar County, where CPS Energy, a municipally owned utility, has actively recruited data center loads through dedicated substations and negotiated rates as part of the city's economic diversification strategy. San Antonio's data center cluster, including Vantage's TX properties, has concentrated on the West and Northwest sides where these incentives apply. CPS Energy's long-range resource planning explicitly flags data centers as a fast-growing load category driving generation and transmission investment through the early 2030s, a signal matched by ERCOT's upward revision of statewide demand forecasts and new interconnection rules under development for large loads.

TX22's standing in Texas data centers is unclear given the absence of a published power figure. Across the state, only 18 of 133 mapped facilities disclose capacity, totaling 468 megawatts. If TX22 follows typical construction-stage disclosure patterns, power and colocation plans may remain unpublished until operational readiness approaches. No certifications or tenant information has been announced.
